page: Microsoft Azure E128s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features dedicated hardware powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. It provides 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with two threads per core running at 4.2 GHz. Memory allocation stands at 1024.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor is configured with 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX matrix accelerators. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options such as Premium Storage.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded and computational throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 122576.45 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 126826.65, both placing in the upper performance tiers. Parallel processing strengths extend to high-throughput tasks, evident in a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 704.78 GB/sec and a static web serving throughput of 165.05 GB/sec. In-memory data structures perform effectively, recorded at 189.85 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference is also notable, delivering 45.31 tokens/sec on prompt processing for a 70B parameter model.

The primary tradeoff of the E128s_v7 lies in its complete reliance on remote storage volumes and moderate single-core benchmark categories. PassMark memory testing registers in the middle tier, showing that the instance is optimized primarily for raw multi-core scaling and memory capacity rather than specialized low-latency memory pipelines. Because it packs 1024 GB of RAM and 128 dedicated execution threads into a single instance footprint, it offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for large monolithic workloads that avoid multi-node clustering overhead.

Given its high core count, comprehensive vector extensions, and 1 TB memory capacity, the E128s_v7 is well suited for enterprise database deployments, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency data analytics workloads.
